newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sheds gains at close,struggles for range.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sheds gains at close,struggles for range.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended little changed on Tuesday after giving up big afternoon gains in the wake of a NYMEX turnaround.
November Brent finished up just 13 cents at $21.73 a barrel after hitting a high of $22.13.
Dealers said crude went into reverse as NYMEX locals elected to take profits after a recovery of Monday's heavy slump ran out of steam.
"The market's been all over the place in the last few days," said an IPE broker. "It's trying to establish a new range."
"Some people got hurt when the market moved on Friday and some got hurt on Monday -- no-one's really sure where this market should be," said another.
Dealers said Middle East events still were casting a shadow over the market.
Prices were pushed higher with news from Washington that extra U.S. forces had, after all, been ordered to Kuwait.
But the foreign ministers of France and Saudi Arabia urged restraint in the region. The two countries were key members of the U.S. led coalition that drove Iraq out of Kuwait in 1991.
Gas oil found support from the perception that Atlantic Basin markets would continue to struggle to replenish low inventories ahead of the winter.
October gas oil finished up 75 cents a tonne at $214.50 and moved out a $1.25 to $7 over November. The November IPE Brent/gas oil crack spread widened to $5.80 a barrel from $5.50-$5.60 on Monday.
